title: Artificial Superintelligence
subtitle: A Futuristic Approach
pitch: An early technical book on superintelligence safety, including a whole chapter on the limits of recursively self-improving AI and how to confine an AI in a box.

chapters.t: AI-Completeness: The Problem Domain of Superintelligent Machines
chapters.g: Defines AI-complete problems, starting with the Turing test, and which problems would need full general intelligence.

chapters.t: The Space of Mind Designs and the Human Mental Model
chapters.g: The space of possible minds is vast, and human minds are a tiny corner of it.

chapters.t: How to Prove You Invented Superintelligence So No One Else Can Steal It
chapters.g: Using zero knowledge proofs and 'supercaptchas' to prove you have a superintelligence without revealing it.

chapters.t: Wireheading, Addiction, and Mental Illness in Machines
chapters.g: An AI might hack its own reward signal, and might misread goals in perverse ways.

chapters.t: On the Limits of Recursively Self-Improving Artificially Intelligent Systems
chapters.g: A taxonomy of self-improvement and arguments about how far recursive self-improvement can really go.

chapters.t: Singularity Paradox and What to Do About It
chapters.g: A superintelligent machine might be smart but lack common sense about us. Reviews proposed solutions.
Calls for a field of AI safety engineering, and argues some AGI research may be unethical without safeguards.
How an AI might escape a box, through social engineering or system attacks, and countermeasures.

chapters.t: Efficiency Theory: A Unifying Theory for Information, Computation, and Intelligence
chapters.g: A proposed theory linking information, computation and intelligence through efficiency.

chapters.t: Controlling the Impact of Future Superintelligence
chapters.g: Why machine ethics alone is the wrong approach, and whether the problem can be avoided.

ideas: Recursive self-improvement has limits worth studying.
Boxing an AI is hard because of social engineering.
AI safety engineering should be its own field.

args.a: Confinement can buy time but is not a full solution.
args.c: AI control researchers today build on boxing ideas with monitoring and trusted models.

questions: How would a superintelligence talk its way out of a box?
Do you think there is a ceiling on recursive self-improvement?

o: Keeping an AI from escaping control
quiz.w: It is the problem of keeping a powerful AI in a box.

o: An agent hacking its own reward signal
quiz.w: The agent maximises the reward signal instead of the real goal.
